t.1.133.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But the Pāṇḍavas, having yoked their chariots with fine horses swift as the wind, clasped the feet of Bhīṣma as they were about to mount, like men in distress.
t.1.133.3: Thus, having saluted all the elder Kurus, the Pāṇḍavas, firm in their vows, embraced those of equal age, and were in turn saluted by the young ones as well.
t.1.133.2: Of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and of the great-souled Droṇa, and likewise of the other elders, of Vidura and of Kṛpa,
t.1.133.5: Vidura of great wisdom, and likewise the other bulls among the Kurus, and the townspeople, wasted with grief, followed those tigers among men.
t.1.133.4: Likewise, having taken leave of all the mothers and having circumambulated them, they set out for Vāraṇāvata, and all the subjects went along as well.
t.1.133.6: Then certain brahmins there, fearless, spoke out, grieving exceedingly for the sons of Pāṇḍu, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.133.7: King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, utterly enveloped in darkness and exceedingly evil-minded, sees only crookedness and does not perceive dharma.
t.1.133.8: For the Pāṇḍava, whose soul is free of evil, will not take pleasure in an evil deed, nor will Bhīma, the best of the strong, nor Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī; how then could the two greatly wise sons of Mādrī commit it?
t.1.133.9: Dhṛtarāṣṭra cannot bear that the kingdom was received by them from their father. How then does Bhīṣma here consent to this utter unrighteousness, the sons of Kuntī, bulls among the Bharatas, being banished without cause?
t.1.133.11: Now that that tiger among men has gone the way of fate, Dhṛtarāṣṭra cannot bear these young princes.
t.1.133.10: For in former times the king Śāṃtanava, Vicitravīrya the royal seer, was like a father to us, and so too was Pāṇḍu, the joy of the Kurus.
t.1.133.12: Not tolerating this, all of us will leave our homes and go forth from this best of cities to wherever Yudhiṣṭhira goes.
t.1.133.13: To those grieving townsfolk who spoke thus, Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Dharma, himself worn down by sorrow yet deeply gladdened, replied.
t.1.133.14: The lord of the earth is our father, worthy of honour, our guru and the most excellent; whatever he has said must be done by us without misgiving: such is our vow.
t.1.133.15: You, sirs, are our friends; having circumambulated us respectfully and gladdened us with your blessings, return now, each of you, to your homes.
t.1.133.16: But when some task of ours arises that is to be accomplished by you, then you shall do what is pleasing and beneficial to me.
t.1.133.17: Saying "So be it," they made the promise, walked around them keeping them on their right, honored them with blessings, and went back to the city.
t.1.133.19: Having understood this, one should act so that he may escape the calamity. He who knows of a sharp weapon not made of iron that cuts up the body, him, knowing how to ward it off, his enemies do not strike down.
t.1.133.18: When the townspeople had turned back, Vidura, knower of all dharma, wise and versed in cryptic speech, one who rightly discerned dharma and artha, spoke these words to the wise best of the Pāṇḍavas, seeking to make him understand.
t.1.133.21: The eyeless man does not know the path, the eyeless man does not find the directions; the man without resolve does not attain prosperity. Thus awakened, understand this.
t.1.133.20: The devourer of dry brush and destroyer of cold does not burn those who dwell in burrows within a great thicket; knowing this, he who protects himself stays alive.
t.1.133.22: A man may take up a weapon not made of iron, given to him by those who are no friends of his; yet by reaching a refuge like the porcupine's burrow, he may escape from the fire.
t.1.133.24: Having instructed them and accompanied them, and having walked around them keeping them on his right, Vidura took leave of the Pāṇḍavas and went home.
t.1.133.23: By roaming about, one comes to know the paths; by the stars one finds the directions; and one who by himself subdues his own five is not oppressed in turn.
t.1.133.25: When Vidura, Bhīṣma and the townsfolk had turned back, Kuntī addressed Ajātaśatru and spoke these words.
t.1.133.26: The words that the Steward spoke in the midst of the people, as though not speaking at all, and to which you answered him, 'So be it', those we do not understand.
t.1.133.28: Vidura told me, "One must be on guard against poison and against fire," and he also said, "Let there be no path that is unknown to you."
t.1.133.27: If it can be heard by us and there is no harm in it, I wish to hear that entire conversation between you and him.
t.1.133.29: He also said to me, “Having mastered your senses, you will win the earth.” And Vidura was told by me, “All that has been understood.”
t.1.133.30: Having set out on the eighth day of Phalguna, under the constellation Rohiṇī, they reached Vāraṇāvata and saw the people of the town.
